where this archive has met it: The ordinary form in the Rio de la Plata, and the spelling this register uses as its own.
what it is, and what it cost or gave: *** THE BASELINE, AND THE REASON THE REST OF THIS TABLE EXISTS: *** every sweep this archive ran for its first month was run on LERENA, and the rows below are what that missed.

where this archive has met it: *** Sancho LLERENA *** of Canelones, 1791-1812, and the town of Llerena in Badajoz. And in one Buenos Aires probate of 1889 the SAME MAN is written *** 'el Doctor LERENA' *** and *** 'el Curador Don LLERENA' ***, twice each, in one hand.
what it is, and what it cost or gave: *** A REAL SPELLING, NOT AN ERROR *** - toponymic from the Extremaduran town, and the commoner form in Spain. *** THE 1889 PASSAGE IS THE CLEAREST PROOF THIS REGISTER HAS THAT THE TWO ARE ONE NAME ***, because one clerk used both in one paragraph about one man.

where this archive has met it: *** 'Avelino SERENA' and 'Adelina SERENA' *** on one 1879 cathedral act; *** 'Maria SERENA' *** on the 1865 Costales marriage; *** 'Mauricio SERENA y Casimira Montano' *** on Cipriano's of 1875; and the Trinidad diagram of 1858, which writes *** 'Ramon SERENA' *** at its apex.
what it is, and what it cost or gave: *** THE S-FOR-L, AND THE MOST EXPENSIVE VARIANT IN THIS ARCHIVE. *** Trinidad had been swept twice on LERENA. A sweep on SERENA, 12 October 2026, returned *** children for two couples this archive had worked for weeks and had no children for *** - Custodio Lerena with Ema Cardozo of the 1911 dispensation, and Juan Bernardo Lerena Pelaez with Eduviges Pelaez of 1894.

where this archive has met it: The same Trinidad volumes, with a tilde.
what it is, and what it cost or gave: *** NOT A SEPARATE SEAM, AND WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU SPEND A DAY ON IT. *** A search for SEREÑA returns the *** IDENTICAL 290 RECORDS *** as SERENA: FamilySearch normalises the n-tilde. *** NO TILDE VARIANT OF THIS NAME NEEDS ITS OWN SWEEP. ***

where this archive has met it: *** 'Abuelos paternos FELIZ GERENA y ROSALIA AGUILAR' *** on the 1811 baptism of Sancho's son Luis Escolastico - in the same sentence that calls the father *** LLERENA ***. Also the unresolved *** 'Dona Andugara GERENA' *** in the Rosario confirmations, and *** 'Doroteo GERENA' *** at Trinidad in 1934.
what it is, and what it cost or gave: *** THE G-FOR-L, DOCUMENTED HERE SINCE 1811 AND STILL PRODUCING PEOPLE. *** The sweep of 12 October 2026 found *** VENANCIO ***, the first child this archive has ever located of either marriage of Alejandro Lerena the younger, and a fifth child for Cipriano.

where this archive has met it: the surname of a father on his daughter's 1899 marriage, *** 'Bernabe PERENA' ***, and *** 'Pio C. PERENA' *** - the same man written *** 'Pio C. SERENA' *** in the companion volume.
what it is, and what it cost or gave: *** THE P-FOR-L. *** Gave *** AMABELIA ***, a fourth child for Cipriano Lerena and Lauriana Beloqui, dead at nineteen in 1899. *** PERENA IS ALSO A SURNAME IN ITS OWN RIGHT ***, so a Perena is a lead and not a relative until an act says otherwise.

where this archive has met it: *** 'ALEXANDRO LEREÑA' *** on his own marriage act at San Jose, 16 September 1825, and *** 'Alberto LEREÑA' *** on the Montevideo cathedral act of 1879.
what it is, and what it cost or gave: *** THE TILDE ADDED RATHER THAN DROPPED ***, and in both cases by the priest writing the act himself - *** so this one is not a transcriber's error at all, but how the family's name was sometimes written down at the font. ***

where this archive has met it: *** 'Avelino LEVENA' *** as godfather on the same 1879 cathedral act that writes the child's father LEREÑA and her grandfather SERENA.
what it is, and what it cost or gave: *** CALLED 'AN EIGHTH SPELLING' IN THIS REGISTER WHEN IT WAS FOUND. *** That one act carries *** FOUR SPELLINGS OF ONE FAMILY'S NAME ON ONE PAGE ***, which is the single best illustration on this page of why a search by letter fails.

where this archive has met it: *** 'Alejandro LORENA' and 'Antonina LORENA' *** in the Cura Vicario's kinship diagram of 1858; *** 'Custodio LORENA' *** on a death of 1981; and Pablo Armando himself, indexed as *** 'ARMAND[O] LORENA' ***.
what it is, and what it cost or gave: *** THE VARIANT THAT ALMOST LOST THE CENTRAL RECORD. *** Pablo Armando's army enrolment card - the document this whole archive turns on - was written off on four objections while it sat under LORENA, and recovered on 10 September 2026. *** A CORRECTION IS LOGGED FOR IT. ***

where this archive has met it: *** 'Bernabe LERESA' *** in the transcript of the 1858 Trinidad diagram.
what it is, and what it cost or gave: *** THE PLATE SAYS LERENA. *** One of five spellings on that single folio - Serena, Lorena, Lorena, Leresa and, four lines above in prose, Lerena correctly. *** THE DIAGRAM IS THE REASON THIS ARCHIVE STOPPED TRUSTING A TRANSCRIPT'S SPELLING AT ALL. ***

where this archive has met it: Fourteen people in the register under the A-spelling (three of them wives of a Larena) in Santa Fe and Entre Rios, 1837-1913, and the Gualeguaychu households.
what it is, and what it cost or gave: *** A SPELLING THAT IS SOMETIMES THIS FAMILY AND SOMETIMES AN ITALIAN NAME. *** At Cayasta it is an Italian colony's LARENA and not ours - a correction is logged - while in Entre Rios it shadows the Lerena Diaz. *** THE ONLY VARIANT ON THIS PAGE THAT HAS TO BE DECIDED CASE BY CASE. ***

where this archive has met it: Four arrivals of 1889, written off as Italian - and then an ORIGINAL act of October 1833 naming *** 'FRANCISCO LERINA y Maria Fernandez' ***.
what it is, and what it cost or gave: *** THIS ARCHIVE EXCLUDED IT AND HAD TO TAKE THAT BACK. *** The exclusion rested on the reasoning that Lerina is an Italian surname; an original parish act then used it for a family with a Maria Fernandez in it. *** A CORRECTION IS LOGGED. ***

where this archive has met it: One full-text hit in the Colombian Catholic records.
what it is, and what it cost or gave: *** NOT PURSUED AND NOT OURS *** - recorded so that the next reader who meets it does not have to decide again.

where this archive has met it: Buenos Aires probate transcripts: *** 'admitio absolutamente LA LERENA' ***, *** 'verificarse LA LERENCIA' ***, *** 'non lerena rece en el' ***.
what it is, and what it cost or gave: *** NOT A SPELLING OF THE NAME AT ALL. IT IS THE SPANISH WORD FOR INHERITANCE. *** In a corpus made entirely of probate files, the commonest word in the corpus impersonates this surname - which is why '700 Argentine hits for Lerena' was never 700 appearances of a rare name. *** THE RULE IT GAVE: before trusting a full-text count, find out what your surname is a MISREADING OF, in that language and that document type. ***
